scheme_name: Fish Extension, Research, and Training Scheme
description:
The Fish Extension, Research, and Training Scheme is an initiative by the Government of India aimed at enhancing the fishery sector in the country. 

This scheme was launched in 2000 under the Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying. 

The primary objective of the scheme is to promote sustainable fish farming practices among fish farmers. 

It aims to increase fish production and productivity through scientific methods. 

The scheme also focuses on improving the socio-economic conditions of fish farmers. 

One of the measurable targets of the scheme is to increase fish production to 22 million metric tons by 2022. 

The scheme aims to enhance the income of fish farmers by 30 percent over a period of five years. 

The benefits under this scheme include financial assistance for adopting modern aquaculture practices. 

Fish farmers can receive up to INR 1 lakh as a subsidy for setting up fish farming units. 

The scheme also provides training programs for fish farmers to improve their skills and knowledge. 

These training programs cover various aspects of fish farming including breeding, feeding, and disease management. 

Eligibility for the scheme includes individuals or groups engaged in fish farming. 

There is no specific age limit for applicants under this scheme. 

However, applicants must have a minimum educational qualification of Class 8. 

The income criteria for eligibility are set at a maximum annual income of INR 2 lakh. 

The application process involves submitting a proposal to the local fisheries department. 

Applicants must provide documents such as identity proof, income certificate, and land ownership documents. 

The proposal must outline the intended fish farming activities and the expected outcomes. 

Once the proposal is submitted, it is reviewed by the local fisheries officer. 

If approved, the applicant is notified and provided with the necessary financial assistance. 

The disbursement of funds typically occurs within three months of approval. 

The scheme operates on a continuous basis with no specific deadlines for application submission. 

Training programs are conducted throughout the year at various locations across the country. 

The implementing authority for the scheme is the Department of Fisheries under the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying. 

State fisheries departments also play a crucial role in the implementation of the scheme. 

They are responsible for conducting training programs and providing technical support to fish farmers. 

The scheme has been instrumental in increasing fish production in India. 

According to the National Fisheries Development Board, fish production increased from 5.5 million metric tons in 2000 to 9.07 million metric tons in 2020. 

This represents a growth rate of approximately 65 percent over two decades. 

The scheme has also contributed to the creation of employment opportunities in the fisheries sector. 

It is estimated that the fisheries sector provides direct employment to over 14 million people in India. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of sustainable fishing practices. 

It encourages fish farmers to adopt environmentally friendly methods of aquaculture. 

The training programs include modules on sustainable fish farming techniques. 

Farmers are educated on the importance of maintaining water quality and biodiversity. 

The scheme has received positive feedback from beneficiaries across various states. 

Many fish farmers have reported increased yields and improved income levels. 

The government has also introduced various awareness campaigns to promote the scheme. 

These campaigns aim to reach out to potential beneficiaries and inform them about the benefits available. 

The scheme aligns with the National Policy on Fisheries which was adopted in 2019. 

This policy aims to achieve a sustainable and responsible fisheries sector in India. 

The Fish Extension, Research, and Training Scheme is a crucial component of this policy. 

It supports the overall goal of enhancing fish production and ensuring food security. 

The scheme also encourages the use of technology in fish farming. 

Farmers are trained in the use of modern equipment and techniques. 

This includes the use of aerators, water quality testing kits, and feed management systems. 

The government also collaborates with various research institutions to improve fish farming practices. 

Research findings are disseminated to fish farmers through training programs and workshops. 

The scheme has also been instrumental in promoting fish exports from India. 

India is currently one of the top fish producers in the world. 

The fisheries sector contributes approximately 1.1 percent to the national GDP. 

The government aims to increase this contribution through various initiatives including this scheme. 

The Fish Extension, Research, and Training Scheme is a comprehensive approach to improving the fisheries sector. 

It addresses various challenges faced by fish farmers including access to technology and market linkages. 

The scheme also promotes the establishment of fish cooperatives. 

These cooperatives help farmers in collective marketing and reducing costs. 

The government provides support for the formation of these cooperatives under the scheme. 

Overall, the Fish Extension, Research, and Training Scheme is a vital initiative for the development of the fisheries sector in India. 

It aims to empower fish farmers and improve their livelihoods through sustainable practices. 

The scheme has a significant impact on food security and economic development in rural areas. 

Through continuous support and training, the government aims to transform the fisheries sector in India. 

The scheme is a testament to the government's commitment to enhancing the livelihoods of fish farmers. 

It plays a crucial role in achieving the broader goals of economic growth and sustainable development.
